# A diagnostic over perl 5.42's lib that perl itself warns or dies on, and so
# is admitted beyond lib_baseline.txt: the privlib-relative diagnostic, a tab,
# and the line perl -w prints calling into the real lib file's own code (not
# a `-e`/minimal-repro script reimplementing the construct inline), copied
# verbatim.
#
# issue 01a156e4 (narrow undef after ref/defined/blessed guards) removed the
# entries the narrowing now sees through: a `ref($x)` truthy guard (plain,
# `&&` short-circuit, `unless ... return`, an if/elsif chain whose earlier
# branch consumes the falsy value), the same for a named array's
# literal-index element and for $_, a dominating arrow deref of the
# argument (vars.go's narrowDerefBase), reftype/refaddr/encode/qualify
# declared as multis by argument type, and types.Select's own Unknown
# bypass and coercion retry (select.go) no longer discarding an argument
# that already decides the call just because another argument does not.
#
# perigrin's ruling (2026-10-20, "possible-undef unless proven") made
# WarnPossibleUndef's default silence general: an Undef from a declared
# return is possible-undef unless the call's own arguments prove the
# Undef-returning candidate selected, covering a single declared candidate
# (Scalar::Util::blessed's one signature, `(Any $ref) Str|Undef`, and
# Cwd::realpath's, `(Str $path) Str|Undef`) exactly as it covers a multi's
# widest, catch-all candidate (Scalar::Util::reftype, refaddr). Only a
# resolved return that is Undef outright, with no other bit at all --
# List::Util::sum's `()` candidate, the only one zero arguments admit --
# still reports unconditionally (markPossibleUndef, calls.go). The mark
# carries from a declared call onto the variable its result is assigned to
# (Symbol.PossibleUndef, ops.go's narrow), so `my $x = f(); ... $x eq
# "..."` silences the same way `f() eq "..."` does.
#
# This removed every remaining line the previous audit (2026-10-20) found:
# the twelve re-measured with real lib-path evidence, and the twelve found
# unreachable by ordinary perl semantics upon inspection (a guard the
# construct's own code already establishes, just not one psc's narrowing
# recognizes) -- CPAN::Distribution::store_persistent_state,
# File::Temp::_deferred_unlink and cleanup, Test2::Compare::Base::clone,
# Test2::Workflow::Task::clone, Test2::API::InterceptResult::Event::init
# and ::clone, Test2::Mock's `ref_copy` constructor, Test::Builder's
# `parent`/`child`, Test::Builder.pm/Test2::API.pm's `blessed($x) &&
# blessed($x) eq ...`, Test2::IPC::Driver::Files::event_file,
# Test2::Util::Ref::rtype, and Test2::Workflow::Task's line-filter --
# none is a lib_baseline.txt entry, and none is listed below, any more.
#
# What is left is Sys::Syslog's own `_syslog_send_console`: `/dev/console`
# is root-only (measured: permission denied for this account), so its
# `open(CONS, ">/dev/console")` can fail honestly in the lib's own
# ordinary use, but reproducing that exact failure needs root. The
# measurement below instead overrides CORE::GLOBAL::open to let the real
# code's own open() succeed without touching the filesystem, leaving CONS
# a filehandle the real code's own `print CONS ...` then finds closed --
# the same fault (a console print failing) the code already defends
# against, from a non-root account.
x86_64-linux-thread-multi/Sys/Syslog.pm:562:19: error: call to POSIX::_exit: argument 1 expects Boolean|Int, got Undef|Boolean [coercion-mismatch]	Use of uninitialized value in subroutine entry at /home/perigrin/.local/share/pvm/versions/5.42.0/lib/perl5/5.42.0/x86_64-linux-thread-multi/Sys/Syslog.pm line 562.
